moat_against: Siemens Healthineers (photon-counting CT lead), Philips, Canon and low-cost United Imaging contest every sale
No proven pricing power — revenue CAGR ~4% and OE/share down over the last 2 years
Hospital capital budgets are cyclical and budget-constrained
US-China tariff exposure and choppy China demand
Patient Care Solutions declining (-13.3% in Q2 2026) and under strategic review
Leverage and acquisition load (Intelerad, pending SOFIE) limit flexibility
moat_for: Large installed imaging base with service and upgrade attach
Broadest modality portfolio (CT, MRI, ultrasound, molecular imaging)
Pharmaceutical Diagnostics consumables — recurring contrast/radiopharmaceutical revenue, +15.6% in Q2 2026
Record backlog $23.9B and book-to-bill 1.15x in Q2 2026
High FDA/regulatory barriers and hospital workflow integration / switching costs
Leading AI clearance portfolio and Edison/CareIntellect software layer on the installed base
moat_justification: Moderate moat (6/10): huge installed imaging base, service attach, broadest modality portfolio and Pharmaceutical Diagnostics consumables give real switching costs and recurring revenue, and the regulatory/FDA barrier is high. But Siemens Healthineers, Philips, Canon and United Imaging contest every modality, hospital capex is cyclical, pricing power is unproven (revenue CAGR ~4%, OE/share CAGR 2y negative), and tariffs/China and PCS weakness erode returns. CAP 9.8 years.
name: GE HealthCare Technologies Inc.
one_liner: Solid, moderate-moat (6/10) imaging franchise with recurring service/PDx revenue, but slow ~4% growth and 4.0x net debt leave it well short of 15% at $68.13 — weighted IRR 7.31%, IV@15% $25.84; it would need to fall toward $25.84 to clear 15%.
